summary: Procurement + security kick-off focusing on MSA/DPA exceptions, SLA targets, KMS/egress constraints, and pilot acceptance criteria. Agreed next steps include MSA redline, technical deep dive on VPC and KMS, and a bench plan for latency/cost verification.
transcript:
Meeting header: 2025-07-17 15:00 UTC | Duration 42m | Recorded by Fireflies
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Carlos Ruiz (Redwood SE), Jenna Patel (Procurement - NimbleHealth), Marcus Lee (InfoSec), Samir Khan (CTO), Olivia Brooks (Legal)
[00:00] Maya: Hey everybody, thanks for joining on a Thursday afternoon. I think we have about 40 minutes, we'll try to keep tight. Quick roll call?
[00:12] Jenna: Hi this is Jenna, procurement.
[00:15] Marcus: Marcus from infosec here.
[00:18] Samir: Samir, CTO.
[00:20] Olivia: Olivia, legal.
[00:22] Carlos: And Carlos Ruiz, solutions engineer at Redwood.
[00:28] Maya: Great. Purpose of today's workshop is to align on the onboarding path, call out any DPA/MSA exceptions, and get technical acceptance criteria for the pilot. We'll cover sla expectations, KMS/egress, and pricing approval flow.
[00:45] Jenna: High level, procurement wants to make sure pricing banding and commit levels are mapped to our fiscal calendar. Also need the standard MSA with DPA attached — our legal has a few flagged clauses.
[00:57] Olivia: Right, primary concerns: data residency clauses, subprocessing list, and indemnity caps. We followed the redline you sent but there are three exceptions we'd like to discuss.
[01:10] Maya: Okay can you bullet them? Also we'll point to our security pack in parallel — SOC2 report and architecture diagram.
[01:18] Olivia: Sure. One: we want tighter egress controls for PHI — explicit contract language around data in transit and at rest and KMS ownership. Two: we want a defined retention window and cert that logs and transcripts can be purged. Three: a right to audit with reasonable notice.
[01:36] Marcus: From security, the KMS question is big. We need to know whether Redwood will support customer-managed keys (CMKs) in a VPC/private deployment or if the hosted will have bring-your-own-key via an HSM integration. Also, can you confirm the encryption-at-rest standard and key rotation?
[01:55] Carlos: Quick clarifier — we support both patterns: Redwood Private (VPC) can be configured to use a customer's KMS/HSM (we call it customer-key integration). For hosted, we currently offer BYOK via our KMS bridge with audited HSM providers, but there are egress logs to be careful about. I should say altho the docs call it Redwood Private, sometimes the product name shows as Redwoood Dedicate in older docs, sorry for confusion.
[02:15] Samir: So for a pilot we probably want the VPC path with CMKs if we are pushing PHI. Can you estimate timeline and cost delta to enable that?
[02:28] Carlos: For Dedicated capacity + customer-managed key in a private network, typical onboarding is 4-6 weeks, cost incremental maybe ~15-25% on baseline depending on reserved capacity and ingress/egress patterns. We'll put together a clearer TCO sheet.
[02:46] Jenna: On pricing approvals — our finance requires a banded structure so that if usage grows we have a predictable step-up without renegotiation every month. Do you have SKU level pricing?
[02:59] Maya: Yes we'll share a pricing spreadsheet — it will include hosted per-token tiers, and Dedicated reserved capacity proposals with committed monthly usage and burst. We can add a clause for tiered pricing escalator tied to usage thresholds.
[03:12] Olivia: Back to the MSA: indemnity cap — your template has a standard cap but our counsel marked it as too low for our requirements. Is there flexibility?
[03:25] Maya: We can propose a middle ground — often we accept a mutual cap or an insurance-backed increase for enterprise customers. I'll flag that with legal.
[03:33] Olivia: Okay please put that in writing in the redline.
[03:37] [04:00] Carlos: I want to walk through the pilot acceptance criteria — we typically specify latency SLOs, success criteria on quality, and a cost budget. For latency, what tier are you aiming for? 95th percentile under 200ms for single-turn generation or is that unrealistic for your workload?
[04:18] Samir: Our UI is interactive (clinical search and chat) so lower latency matters. We don't need 95th at 200ms for long sequences, but for typical question-answer it's desirable under 300-350ms p95. Cost is secondary but still important.
[04:33] Carlos: Okay, so p95 300-350ms target. We'll capture sequence length distribution and run a small bench. Note real numbers will vary by model and quantization. We'll suggest a model variant that's tuned for latency.
[04:48] Marcus: Also we require end-to-end audit logs for any transcript or model output flagged as PHI. Where are logs stored and what's the retention?
[04:58] Maya: Logs live in our observability stack with retention tiers — default is 90 days for full-level traces, 1 year for summary metrics; we can extend retention via premium add-on. For transcripts stored as request payloads, we can map to the DPA retention field and offer purge APIs.
[05:17] Marcus: Need that in the DPA language.
[05:20] Maya: Noted.
[05:23] [06:00] Jenna: On vendor risk committee — they'll ask about third-party subprocessors. Do you have an up-to-date subprocessor list?
[06:10] Maya: Yes we maintain a list; I'll attach the up-to-date subprocessor manifest to the follow-up pack. It includes cloud infra partners and telemetry vendors.
[06:20] Olivia: Also export controls and data transfers: we operate in EU and US, some patient data must remain in EU. Do you support region pinning?
[06:31] Carlos: Region pinning is supported in Private and Dedicated; for hosted we can provision region-limited endpoints but there are limitations for replication. If you need strict EU-only residency for data at rest and compute, Private in your region is the recommended path.
[06:50] Samir: For our minimum viable pilot we'd like EU residency for data and a private VPC with CMK. Can you outline the onboarding steps?
[06:59] Carlos: High-level: 1) sign MSA/DPA with residency/KMS clauses 2) network setup (VPC peering/Transit), IP allowlist 3) KMS key exchange and HSM attestations 4) pilot provisioning and bench tests 5) acceptance and rollout. We'll provide a detailed runbook.
[07:20] Maya: How about compliance: you mentioned SOC2 — any other certifications we should call out?
[07:26] Marcus: SOC2 is baseline; we may need HIPAA attestation language given PHI, and possibly ISO27001 evidence. For some regulated contracts FedRAMP would be ideal but not required for this pilot.
[07:40] Carlos: We can provide SOC2 Type II, annual penetration test reports, and our security whitepaper. For HIPAA we have a BAA template we can attach to the MSA.
[07:50] Olivia: Yes please include the BAA language in the redline.
[07:56] [08:30] Jenna: Timeline constraints — procurement needs approved vendor before our Q4 procurement freeze (early Oct). What's realistic?
[08:39] Maya: If we move quickly on redlines and technical prep, we can hit pilot in 6 weeks and initial production in 12-14 weeks, meaning approvals by mid-September would work. But that depends on legal negotiation speed.
[08:55] Olivia: We have internal escalation windows — I can fast-track if the first redline is clean.
[09:00] Maya: Great.
[09:05] [09:30] Carlos: On pricing — we'll prepare both Hosted and Dedicated scenarios: per-token hosted with a discount ladder for volume, and Dedicated with a reserved GPU pool rate + overage. Jenna, finance wanted banding — what kind of commit ranges are you thinking?
[09:47] Jenna: For pilot we're low volume, but for production we'd expect 2-3 million tokens/month in year one and potentially 10M+/month in year two. We need price certainty across that growth.
[09:58] Maya: We'll model both. Also want to call out egress fees if using BYOK with cross-region access, those can impact cost.
[10:08] Marcus: On egress: our procurement policy wants bounded egress costs and a cap or alert mechanism.
[10:15] Maya: We can include a billing alert and set upper-bound thresholds in the contract for first 90 days during pilot.
[10:22] [11:00] Samir: Technical question — what model variants are you proposing that meet the latency/cost tradeoff? We prefer open variants but need Redwood-verified performance.
[11:12] Carlos: We'll propose a curated model from our catalog: one with quantization-friendly weights, lower context cost. For examples, a 7B quantized variant for low-latency chat and a larger 13B for high-quality generating tasks. We'll share perf profiles.
[11:30] Maya: We'll include a performance appendix to the pilot SOW with p95 targets, dataset used for bench and quality acceptance tests.
[11:40] [12:00] Olivia: A couple legal nitpicks — data deletion: we need a contract clause that Redwood will provide certification of deletion upon request and within 30 days of termination.
[12:10] Maya: Thirty days is standard, we can commit to certify with log evidence.
[12:15] Olivia: Also SLA credits — our legal wants a defined credit schedule for unmet SLOs.
[12:22] Maya: We can provide a credit schedule for availability and latency breaches tied to the production Dedicated SLA. Pilot will have softer targets but documented acceptance tests.
[12:35] Marcus: For audit rights, a read-only attestation or SOC2 plus on-site audit with notice — what's the common practice?
[12:45] Carlos: Many customers accept SOC2 + contractual right to request supplementary evidence; on-site audits are rarer, but we can negotiate limited audit rights with predefined scope.
[12:58] [14:00] Jenna: Are there any legal or procurement blockers from Redwood side for our EU data pinning and HSM requirement?
[14:08] Maya: No blockers, but it will require Private/Dedicated and an MSA/DPA with the residency/KMS clauses included. There may be an implementation fee for dedicated infra in a specific region.
[14:20] Samir: Implementation fee is fine if the TCO makes sense. We just want transparency.
[14:25] Maya: We'll include detailed TCO with expected cost delta and a runbook.
[14:33] [15:00] Carlos: One more technical: how do you want us to structure acceptance tests? We recommend a short prompt set with 1000 sample requests representing production distribution, run benchmarks for latency and quality, and tie quality thresholds to BLEU-like or human-checked pass rates.
[15:12] Samir: That works. We'll provide a sample data set (anonymized) and our key user journeys.
[15:20] Marcus: We'll require encryption in transit and at rest confirmed, plus a diagram showing where logs are stored.
[15:28] Carlos: We'll include the network architecture diagram in the security pack and call out zones for logs and retention.
[15:36] [16:00] Olivia: To summarize: redline MSA/DPA with BAA and deletion certs; specify KMS/CMK support and region pinning; pricing banded with commit tiers; SLA credit schedule; pilot SOW with acceptance tests and bench plan.
[16:15] Maya: Yes and action items: I'll send a consolidated follow-up with redline and security pack by Sunday 7/20, Carlos will own the technical runbook and bench plan and schedule the deep dive week of 7/28; Nimble to share regulated data flow map by 7/24.
[16:30] Jenna: That timeline works from procurement side.
[16:35] Samir: Quick question on subprocessors — can you confirm any subcontractors located outside EU?
[16:42] Maya: We'll include the manifest; if there are non-EU subprocessors touching EU data we can discuss contractual scoping so data doesn't leave region.
[16:50] [18:00] Carlos: Minor note - some early docs call our rollback policy 'auto-fallback' to smaller models in the event of capacity constraints; we'll document how fallbacks affect latency and cost.
[18:10] Marcus: We want to ensure fallback doesn't send data to a non-EU region.
[18:16] Carlos: Understood — fallback policies can be region-aware for Private deployments.
[18:22] [19:00] Maya: Any final questions?
[19:04] Olivia: Not from legal — just ensure the redline includes the BAA and deletion certification.
[19:07] Jenna: No further procurement questions.
[19:10] Samir: Good.
[19:14] Maya: Thanks everyone. We'll follow up with the pack and proposed SOW.
[19:20] Meeting end.

Notes: occasional transcription errors present (Redwood product names, some acronyms). Links referenced: "Redwood security pack (link)" "MSA redline draft (link)" "Pricing spreadsheet (link)" — will be attached in follow-up email.
